title: Push two reject cartons off a moving line onto the reject table, leaving the good ones on it
instruction: The two red cartons on the moving line are rejects. Push each one off the line onto the grey reject table behind the line before it reaches the tunnel, and leave the brown cartons on the line.
context: Where a packing line has no automatic diverter, a carton that fails a check (weight, seal, label) is pushed off the running conveyor onto a reject table by the operator beside it, without stopping the line and without disturbing the good cartons riding just in front of and behind it. The cartons are too wide to pick in one hand, so the reject has to be pushed sideways while it moves. Done by: packing-line operators and line-side cobots.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table (1.10 x 1.30 m) whose side edges are 65 cm either side of the midpoint between the bases. A straight conveyor crosses the table parallel to the line through the bases, its centre line 26 cm in front of them, flowing from the robot's right to its left. Two dark steel rails (1.5 x 1.5 cm, 153 cm long) run along it, centred 4 cm either side of the centre line, from 61 cm right of the midpoint to 92 cm left of it. Four grey steel carrier plates (14 cm across the line, 12 cm along it, 1.5 cm thick) ride 2 mm above the rails (their tops 3.2 cm above the table), square to them, centred on the centre line, 13 cm apart centre to centre (1 cm between carriers); at the start their centres are 14, 27, 40 and 53 cm right of the midpoint. On each carrier a closed carton (12 cm across the line, 10 cm along it, 5 cm tall, 200 g) stands square in the middle (3 cm between neighbouring cartons); from the front of the line (the leftmost): brown cardboard, red, brown cardboard, red. Along the far side of the line lies a grey steel reject table top (18 cm deep, from 34 to 52 cm in front of the bases, 1 cm from the carriers' far edge; 96 cm long, from 62 cm right to 34 cm left of the midpoint; its top 2.7 cm above the table, 5 mm below the carriers' tops), with a dark steel fence 1 cm thick standing 3 cm above its top along its far edge and both ends. From 34 cm left of the midpoint the conveyor runs into a grey sheet-steel tunnel: two side walls (1 cm thick, 10.2 cm tall, 58 cm long) whose inner faces are 8.25 cm either side of the centre line, under a 0.8 cm roof whose underside is 2 cm above the cartons' tops, closed at its far end (92 cm left of the midpoint), where it stands on a dark steel post to the floor (18.5 x 4 cm, centred 89 cm left of the midpoint). The belt speeds up to 5 cm/s over the first 0.3 s of the trial, runs at 5 cm/s, and stops (over 0.3 s) at 19.4 s, when every carrier is inside the tunnel. Untouched, the cartons' leading faces reach the tunnel's mouth at 8.8, 11.4, 14.0 and 16.5 s.
scoring: At the end of the trial, with what a per-step monitor recorded over the whole trial: +0.5 for each red carton placed on the reject table: its bottom within 1 cm of the table's top (any face down), its whole footprint on the table (past its near edge, inside its fence), still (under 1 cm/s), no part of either gripper within 4 cm of it plus however far that gripper's fingers are open, and at every control step its centre was over its carrier's footprint or over the reject table's side of the line (from the carriers' far edge to the fence, along the table) with its bottom between 1 cm below the reject table's top and 1 cm above the carriers' tops: pushed straight across, never lifted, never on the station table or the floor. 0 for a red carton anywhere else (on its carrier or in the tunnel, on the station table, on the floor, overhanging the reject table's edge, held or pressed by a gripper, still sliding) or that left that route at any moment, even if later pushed onto the reject table. -0.5 for each brown carton not standing upright on its own carrier (its centre outside the carrier's 14 x 12 cm footprint, or more than 1 cm off the height it rides at) at the end or at any control step during the trial: knocked off or over and put back still counts. The total is never below 0. 1.0 when both red cartons are placed and both brown cartons stood on their carriers all trial (the trial then ends with success once this has held for 1 s); 0.5 for one red carton placed. Pushing every carton onto the table, or sweeping the whole line off, scores 0.
reset_notes: Run the carriers back to their start positions, stand each carton back square in the middle of its carrier (the brown ones may be in the tunnel, the red ones on the reject table), and start the belt with the trial. Safety for real trials: the cartons are empty 200 g cardboard boxes on a 5 cm/s belt, the reject table's 3 cm fence stops a carton pushed too far, and the tunnel's low roof keeps hands and grippers out of the conveyor's end.
fidelity: The carriers follow their path exactly, like a servo-driven conveyor: the arms can't push or stop them. They ride 2 mm above the rails. The cartons are rigid boxes with the station's rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), more than cardboard on steel, and the carriers 0.8 / 0.7; a push even at a carton's top edge slides it rather than tipping it. Reject cartons are red all over rather than carrying a red label, one colour per rigid body.
